title: spec review: S2a1 memory_hot: bounded HOT memory view generated from the store, never-compact classes, deterministic compaction, memory hot/compact CLI (P1 HOT, P4)
spec:
Create orchestrator/memory_hot.py on top of memory_store (S1a). Config in pool.toml [memory]: hot_budget_tokens = 3000 (dated comment; tokens estimated as chars/4 like skills_registry._token_estimate), hot_never_compact = ["gotcha:unresolved", "architecture", "decision:constraint"], hot_recent_days = 14. build(root, budget_tokens=None) -> {"records": [...], "tokens": n, "dropped": [ids], "pinned": [ids]}: candidates = every warm record, read through a new memory_store.all_records(root, tier=None) helper (no limit; add it in memory_store.py, scope below), never through search() whose limit defaults to 20; pinned (never compacted) = architecture records, gotchas whose outcome is empty or says unresolved/open, decisions tagged constraint or security, and any record for which ANY id in its source_tasks list names a bus task whose status is one of queued, held, running (an open-status allowlist; done, failed, superseded, unknown ids and any other value count as closed); the rest ranked by score = recency (days since date, decaying over hot_recent_days) + kind weight (gotcha 3, decision 2, architecture 2, model_note 1, retrospective 1, strategy 1, skill_outcome 1, reference 1) + 1 per open bus task whose title or scope mentions one of the record's components; fill the budget by score after the pinned set; if the pinned set alone exceeds the budget, keep it and report over_budget = true (never drop pinned). Each record is rendered as one compact line (date, kind, title, and for gotchas the first sentence of the body) plus a pointer line 'memory show <id>' only for governing decisions that were dropped. Writes .orchestrator/memory/HOT.md with a first line stating it is generated by memory_hot and must not be edited, and marks the chosen records tier hot in the store (all others hot -> warm; cold unchanged). compact(root) = build and rewrite; idempotent. CLI: `orchestrator memory hot [--json]` (prints the view and the budget report), `orchestrator memory compact` (rebuilds HOT.md, prints pinned/dropped counts). Run migrate + compact against this repository's real memory files and report the token count and the pinned/dropped counts in the result and in docs/hermes-hardening/07-hot-memory.md. Do not touch spawn.py: packets are wired in the next task.
Spec review T-1064 folded in: open-status allowlist for pinning on ANY source_tasks id; reference weight 1; unbounded candidate read via memory_store.all_records; the merged Record field is source_tasks (list).
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_pinned_classes_never_dropped (unresolved gotcha, architecture, constraint decision and open-task records survive a tiny budget with over_budget true)
tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_budget_fill_by_score_and_tier_marks (higher-score records chosen first; store tiers updated; HOT.md written with the generated header)
tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_pinning_uses_open_status_allowlist_on_any_source_task (superseded and unknown ids do not pin; a running one does)

risks.issue: Default hot_never_compact = ["gotcha:unresolved", "architecture", "decision:constraint"] does not match the prose pin rule 'gotchas whose outcome is empty or says unresolved/open, decisions tagged constraint or security'. The config is missing decision:security entirely and collapses three gotcha conditions (empty outcome, 'unresolved', 'open') into one tag. With only the defaults wired up, a security-tagged decision or a gotcha with an empty/'open' outcome will not be pinned unless the executor hardcodes extra logic outside the config, defeating the point of making this configurable and silently under-protecting exactly the records the spec calls governing.

Acceptance test test_pinned_classes_never_dropped only lists 'unresolved gotcha, architecture, constraint decision and open-task records' — it never exercises a security-tagged decision or a gotcha with an empty/'open' outcome, so the config/prose mismatch above is not caught by the gate. Acceptance criteria as written can pass while the security-tag and empty/open-outcome pin paths are silently broken.

Spec requires build()/compact() to 'mark the chosen records tier hot in the store' and flip others 'hot -> warm', but memory_store currently has no tier-mutation function (tier is write-once inside _make_record at migration time) and 'hot' is not a value the store has ever produced (only warm/cold, per docs/hermes-hardening/01-memory-store.md). The spec explicitly calls out adding all_records() but never names this second required store-level addition (e.g. a set_tier(root, ids, tier) function), so the insertion point is left to be improvised.

docs/hermes-hardening/01-memory-store.md states 'memory rebuild discards the database and recreates it solely from Markdown,' which resets every record's tier back to warm/cold via _make_record. The spec never mentions that this silently wipes all 'hot' markings written by compact(), nor requires re-running compact after rebuild. This is a state-that-silently-resets footgun a reviewer would flag if undocumented.

The open-status allowlist description lists 'done, failed, superseded, unknown ids' as closed, but bus.STATUSES only ever contains {queued, held, running, done, failed} — 'superseded' cannot occur as a real bus task status, and 'unknown ids' is ambiguous between a literal status value and a source_task id absent from the bus entirely (the acceptance test name 'superseded and unknown ids do not pin' suggests both are meant to be exercised as fixture data, not real bus states). This ambiguity risks the executor testing a codepath that can never trigger via the real bus API while missing the actual 'id not found' case.

Scoring rule '+1 per open bus task whose title or scope mentions one of the record's components' does not define match semantics (case sensitivity, substring vs whole-word), which affects determinism of test_budget_fill_by_score_and_tier_marks across implementations.

New hot_* keys are added into the existing [memory] table, which already holds unrelated progressive-recall packet keys (budget_hits, min_score, budget_chars, packet_layers). Not a functional bug (TOML doesn't allow a second [memory] header, so the merge is correct), but 'budget_chars' next to 'hot_budget_tokens' invites confusion between the two unrelated budgets — worth a comment separating the two feature blocks.

suggested_spec_changes: Fix hot_never_compact default to cover every pinned class named in prose, e.g. ["gotcha:unresolved", "gotcha:open", "architecture", "decision:constraint", "decision:security"], and state explicitly that a gotcha with an empty outcome pins unconditionally (not via a config string) so there's one source of truth instead of two.
Add acceptance coverage for the decision:security tag and for a gotcha with an empty outcome, not just 'unresolved', so the config/prose mismatch above cannot silently regress.
Name the new memory_store.py tier-mutation entry point explicitly (e.g. set_tier(root, ids, tier)) alongside all_records() so the executor doesn't improvise the storage insertion point.

Document that `orchestrator memory rebuild` resets all tiers to warm/cold and that `memory compact` must be rerun afterward to restore hot markings; note this in docs/hermes-hardening/07-hot-memory.md.

Clarify that 'unknown ids' means a source_tasks id with no matching bus task at all (not a literal status string), and either drop 'superseded' from the closed-status enumeration or note it is a forward-compatible placeholder not reachable through today's bus.STATUSES, so test fixtures know to write it directly rather than via the public bus API.
Specify the exact component-mention matching rule (e.g. case-insensitive whole-word match against record.components) used for the +1 open-bus-task score bonus.
